t: You're looking at Somerset House, a large neoclassical complex on the south side of the Strand, overlooking the Thames just east of Waterloo Bridge. The Georgian quadrangle stands on the site of a Tudor palace that belonged to Edward Seymour, the first Duke of Somerset. Sir William Chambers designed the present building, begun in 1776, and he was a founder member of the Royal Academy. The Victorian wings to east and west were added in 1831 and 1856. Until the Victoria Embankment was built in the late 1860s, the river ran right up against the building.
